newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan back in the corn market in earnest.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan back in the corn market in earnest.

text.p: Taiwanese buyers are expected to return to the U.S. corn market in earnest next week after a resumption of purchases this week following a gap in trading throughout August, local dealers said on Friday.
State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp is expected to tender later in the week for a combined shipment of 30,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and soybeans, they said.
Traders said Taiwan Sugar was also expected to tender on September 13 for another 10,000-tonne corn shipment.
Besides the Taiwan Sugar tenders, another two Taiwan groups are seen to be in the market for corn supplies, traders said.

Taiwan's Members Feed Industry Group will be seeking a 54,000-tonne corn shipment for its late November supplies, while the FGEP group is in the market for a 54,000-tonne corn shipment, but has yet to decide on delivery dates.

Taiwan buyers appear to regard current world corn prices as fair, a trader said. Many buyers are being tempted to move up their tender schedules after seeing Japan and South Korea move to lay in first-quarter 1997 corn, he said.
"Corn buying interest is quite strong this week and that prompted many Taiwan buyers to consider tenders," he said.
Taiwan interests bought a total of 76,000 tonnes of U.S. corn and 10,000 tonnes of U.S. soybeans at tenders last week.
Taiwan's domestic soymeal price on Friday for Taipei delivery was between T$9.60 to T$9.80 a kg, up from T$9.40 to T$9.50 a week earlier.
Corn powders were at T$7.10 to T$7.15 a kg for Taipei delivery, up from T$7.05 to T$7.10 a week earlier.
Local Pacific Northwest freight was quoted about US$11.00 a tonne and Gulf of Mexico freight at about $20.55 to S$21.50 a tonne, both for Panamax-sized November and December shipments.
In the wheat market, traders said the Taiwan Flour Mills Association would remain sidelined in September as the group bought 98,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat at a tender on August 29.
Association official Lu Wei-chih said wheat supplies should last until late October.
Local flour prices listed on Friday for Taipei delivery ranged between T$14.55 to T$15.68 kg, unchanged from a week earlier, but discounts were being given to retailers.
The discounts were possible because the flour prices were based on Taiwan's wheat subsidy fund fixed at $245 a tonne, while import costs have fallen for recent shipments.
The flour association bought on August 29 three shipments totalling 98,000 tonnes of wheat averaging $228 a tonne.
The wheat subsidy fund, established years ago to stabilise prices and ensure supplies, pays wheat buyers for costs beyond a benchmark of $245 a tonne on a cost-and-freight basis.

An official at Taiwan's Council of Agriculture said the government had no plan to lower the wheat subsidy fund benchmark, a policy that will extend the life of the fund as long as wheat prices remain soft.
The government has pledged not to replenish the fund once it runs out. It has T$600 million to T$700 million available.
Taiwan flour prices at factories ranged on Friday between T$12.27 and $12.5 a kg, Lu said.
